validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification/ownership split — well corroborated. Do add the two independent refs staged below (Capacity, Location) and see the separate spec/attribution concerns filed for Length and FuelSource/Operator.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: this is a real, actively-maintained transmission trunk, not a GEM-only entity. Three independent sources confirm it: (1) East European Gas Analysis (eegas.com/belarus1.htm, verified live) lists it in its Belarus pipeline scheme as 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina, 2 x 1220 mm (48-in)', immediately after 'Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi, 3 x 1220 mm' — i.e. this is the downstream continuation of the Torzhok trunk into Ukraine. (2) iSANS's Feb 2023 Belarusian-energy-security report (isans.org PDF, already cited on the sheet for Diameter, verified live+content via pdftotext since url_verifier can't parse PDF bytes) states in its own words: 'Украина и Беларусь связаны двухниточным магистральным газопроводом «Ивацевичи — Долина» диаметром 1220 мм (около 30 млрд куб. м. в год)' — 'Ukraine and Belarus are connected [present tense, 2023] by a twin-thread trunk gas pipeline Ivatsevichi-Dolina, 1220mm diameter, ~30 bcm/y' — explicitly confirming both the route/endpoints and that it is CURRENTLY in service. (3) Beltruboprovodstroy JSC's own customer-reviews page (beltps.com/customer-reviews/, verified) states the contractor completed OVERHAUL works (June-Dec 2018) on 'The Ivatsevichi-Dolina main gas pipeline' for Gazprom Transgaz Belarus — a company performing a capital overhaul on a pipe is strong evidence it was in active service, not abandoned. CAVEAT: GEM's own wiki page for this pipeline opens with 'is a mothballed gas pipeline' — this line directly contradicts (a) the wiki's own data tables two paragraphs later, which list both segments' Status as Operating, and (b) all three independent sources above, none of which describe it as idle/mothballed (isans's 2023 report uses present tense 'связаны'/are connected). The 'mothballed' framing appears to be legacy/stale wiki prose that was never reconciled with the sheet's own Operating status or with the 2018 overhaul evidence. Recommend treating the sheet's Status=operating as correct and, if anyone edits the wiki narrative, dropping the 'mothballed' opening line as unsupported/contradicted. CLASSIFICATION: transmission trunk, correctly classified — matches the description of a large-diameter (1220mm) cross-border trunk continuing from the Torzhok hub into Ukraine's Dolyna gas-transport/storage hub. OWNERSHIP: the sheet's existing Owner split (Owner1=Gazprom PJSC, Owner2=Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine) is CORRECT and matches this sweep's country-specific expectation — Gazprom legitimately owns the Belarusian portion (Beltransgaz/Gazprom Transgaz Belarus has been 100%-Gazprom since 2011), while GTSOU is the Ukrainian state successor holding the Ukrainian portion; this is NOT the 'Gazprom owns 100% of a wholly-Ukrainian row' error pattern this sweep is watching for, because this pipeline is genuinely cross-border (starts in Ivatsevichy, Belarus).

validity.recommendation: No merge/relabel — P3484 (segment I) and P5938 (segment II) are a legitimate parallel two-thread pair, exactly like other Soviet-era twin/triple trunks in this roster. Do not fold one into the other.

Independent sourcing resolves this as a legitimate pair rather than a duplicate: eegas.com's Belarus pipeline scheme explicitly lists 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina, 2 x 1220 mm' (i.e. two physical parallel pipes on one corridor), and iSANS's 2023 report independently calls it a 'двухниточный' (twin-thread) trunk. Search-engine synthesis of a UNECE/ENVSEC Belarus-pipelines environmental-safety assessment (unece.org PDF; could not be independently fetched myself — see the Length concern below for why) consistently returns '2 strings ... built in 1976/1981' for this same pipeline, which lines up exactly with GEM's own StartYear1=1976 for P3484 and would fit P5938 as the 1981 second thread. So: two real, separately-built parallel pipes, matching the guidance's expectation for this corridor (cf. Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi's 3 parallel 1220mm lines feeding this same hub). No merge indicated.

validity.recommendation: Verify LengthKnown against a fetchable authoritative source; current sheet value (292.00 km) is suspect and may need correcting to ~146 km. Do not apply a fix without an independently verifiable citation.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's sheet records LengthKnown=292.00 km for this row (P3484, segment I) and the SAME 292.00 km for P5938 (segment II) — i.e. both parallel threads carry an identical length figure that happens to equal 2x146. GEM's OWN gem.wiki mirror of this exact pipeline (fetched directly, raw HTML, last regenerated 2024-09-16 per the sheet's own 'updated' date, so contemporaneous with the current row) instead shows 'Length: 146 km each' for BOTH segment I and segment II — exactly half the sheet's current value. That wiki figure cites footnote [11] = eegas.com/belarus1.htm, but I fetched eegas.com/belarus1.htm directly (raw HTML) and it contains NO length/km figures at all for this pipeline — only diameter and thread-count ('2 x 1220 mm'). So the wiki's 146 km citation is itself misattributed/unsupported, meaning I cannot confirm 146 km through that chain either. I then tried to reach the likely original source: multiple independent web-search syntheses point to a UNECE/ENVSEC 'Environmental safety of main pipelines in Belarus' assessment (unece.org/sites/default/files/2025-08/_ENG__ENVSEC_EE_pipelines_project_Assessment.pdf) which reportedly states this pipeline is '146 km, 2 strings, 1220mm, built in 1976/1981' — years that match GEM's own StartYear1=1976 exactly, which is a meaningful corroborating detail. However I could NOT independently verify this: the PDF returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge) to both a direct fetch and WebFetch; no Wayback Machine capture exists yet, and a fresh Save Page Now attempt returned 520 (IA cannot reach the origin either) — so per standing rule 2/3 I cannot cite it and have not staged a fill. Net assessment: the sheet's 292 km is unconfirmed and contradicted by GEM's own wiki mirror of the same row (146 km), and the 2x relationship (146x2=292) is exactly the shape of a 'combined two-thread total pasted into a single thread's field' data-entry error. Flagging as a spec concern for a human pass with access to the UNECE PDF (or another route past its Cloudflare challenge) rather than applying an unverified number myself.

validity.recommendation: Re-research FuelSource. 'Urengoy gas field' is very likely anachronistic for a pipeline whose own StartYear1=1976; check whether it should instead be an early West Siberian source (e.g. Medvezhye or Vuktyl, both online well before 1976) or the generic Torzhok trunk-system supply, rather than Urengoy specifically.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records FuelSource='Urengoy gas field' for this row, with StartYear1=1976. Urengoy is one of the world's largest gas fields but its FIRST gas production was 22 April 1978 (confirmed via general web search of standard field histories) — i.e. two years AFTER this pipeline's recorded start year. A pipeline that began operating in 1976 could not have originally been carrying Urengoy gas, because Urengoy gas did not yet exist commercially. The Torzhok hub that feeds this corridor (per eegas.com's Belarus scheme, 'Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi' feeds directly into 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina') was originally supplied by earlier West Siberian/Komi fields (e.g. Medvezhye, online from 1972, or Vuktyl via the Ukhta-Torzhok system) before Urengoy volumes came online in scale in the 1980s. I could not find a citable independent source naming the ACTUAL original fuel source for this specific pipeline, so I am not proposing a replacement value (per standing rule against forcing weak fields) — but 'Urengoy gas field' as currently recorded is very likely wrong given the 1976 start date, and this field currently carries no ref at all (MISSING_REF), so it has never been checked against a source.

This is the COMBINED capacity of the twin-thread system (both P3484 and P5938 together), and it closely matches the sheet's per-row figure of 29 bcm/y (29 vs ~30, within normal rounding for a secondary source). NOTE for a human reviewer: it is not fully clear whether GEM's convention on this row is meant to record the single-thread capacity or the whole-corridor capacity duplicated onto both parallel rows — if the latter, summing P3484+P5938 would overstate true throughput roughly 2x, the same shape as the Length concern filed separately. I am citing this source because it corroborates the VALUE as printed (29≈30), not because it resolves the per-thread-vs-system question; url_verifier cannot parse PDF text directly (it checked HTTP 200 only), so I manually confirmed the '1220 мм' / '30 млрд куб. м.' text via pdftotext -layout on the downloaded PDF.

Two independent sources corroborate the Ivatsevichy(Belarus)->Dolyna(Ukraine) corridor: iSANS 2023 ('Украина и Беларусь связаны ... газопроводом «Ивацевичи — Долина»' — Ukraine and Belarus are connected by the Ivatsevichi-Dolina pipeline) and East European Gas Analysis's Belarus pipeline scheme (eegas.com/belarus1.htm: 'Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi, 3 x 1220mm' feeding into 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina, 2 x 1220mm', consistent with Ivatsevichy as the Belarusian junction point and Dolyna as the Ukrainian terminus/hub). Both verified live via url_verifier (eegas directly; isans PDF confirmed via pdftotext since url_verifier only checks HTTP 200 on PDFs).
